exposure: Antenatal ultrasound suspicion of fetal growth restriction (FGR)
outcome: Admission to neonatal intensive care unit
cohort: Small for gestational age (SGA) infants delivered at ≥28 weeks' gestation (n = 407)
finding: Regular third-trimester ultrasound examinations were associated with increased rates of iatrogenic deliveries in SGA infants suspected of FGR, but not with improved neonatal outcomes except for reduced perinatal resuscitation risk.
mod_finding: Elective caesarean section was higher in the group with antenatal ultrasound suspicion of FGR (aRR 1.306, 95% CI 1.051, 1.623).
